title: Directors who had rock-solid work all the way into old age?

commenti.body:
Schrader had a bit of a lull in the 90s but is making great films again at almost 80. 

Adding more because minimum comment nonsense. Adding more because minimum comment nonsense. Adding more because minimum comment nonsense. Adding more because minimum comment nonsense.

I heard The Card Counter was pretty rough—which is why I’m slightly leery of his late career. I did really like First Reformed though (and I feel like maybe that’s his “defining film” as a director for most young people.
